children: With Friday's 5% selloff, the Nasdaq Composite Index is now down 2.7% for the year and has become the laggard of the major indexes. (The Dow and S&P 500 are narrowly mixed year to date).
Nasdaq is down about 18% from its Oct. 6 peak of 27599.79. A drop of more than 20% from a closing high would put the index in a bear market.

Nasdaq had been in positive territory for 2026 since April 14, according to Dow Jones Market Data. It has spent 173 trading days in positive territory for the year, compared with 50 trading days in negative territory.
